title: A run incarnation that ends without a terminal state leaves no checkpoint record of it
description:
epic-ncv's checkpoint went from sequence 39 ('z23 is running', 2026-09-18 16:39) straight to 40 ('admitted', 16:50), with no failed or stopped state between.

The cause is known, and it was me: I killed the run with SIGTERM at 16:50 to force a re-plan (the g50 workaround). The FEED recorded it — 'run_died: stopped by a signal (terminated)' at 16:50:11. The CHECKPOINT did not. So the durable record the close-out reads says nothing happened, while the ephemeral feed knew exactly what did.

That is backwards: the feed is uncommitted exhaust and the checkpoint is the durable truth.

Work:
- On a catchable signal, write a terminal checkpoint before exiting (the signal handler already records to the feed; record to the checkpoint too).
- For an uncatchable end (SIGKILL, power loss), the NEXT incarnation should record that its predecessor ended without a terminal state, naming the last sequence it saw.
- Either way the gap becomes a counted event for the intervention count rather than an invisible one.

From ncv close-out finding 823d2af9.
acceptance_criteria: Every incarnation's end is recorded in the checkpoint, either by the ending process or by its successor, and a SIGTERM leaves a terminal state
